author: N/A
title: The Old Testament
why_read: The foundational scripture of Western religious, moral, and literary history, containing enduring wisdom literature, poetry, and narrative history.
my_opinion: Incredibly boring and of little value to me. Only books I'd revisit would be proverbs and Eclesiastes.

author: John Yates (Culadasa), Matthew Immergut & Jeremy Graves
title: The Mind Illuminated
why_read: A clear, stage-by-stage manual combining Buddhist shamatha-vipassana meditation with modern cognitive neuroscience.
my_opinion: Halfway reading it.

author: Keith Ferrazzi
title: Never Eat Alone
why_read: A practical guide to building meaningful, reciprocal relationships and networking based on genuine generosity rather than transactional schmoozing.

author: Marcus Aurelius
title: The Meditations of Marcus Aurelius
why_read: Private reflections of a Roman emperor on maintaining duty, humility, mental resilience, and tranquility amidst chaos.
my_opinion: Incredible paralelisms with budism. The beauty of stoicism in understanding life, and centering yourself on what really matters. How current this book is, and how sad that is with regards to the evolution of humanity's understanding of life.

author: James Allen
title: As a Man Thinketh
why_read: A short, timeless classic arguing that your thoughts directly shape character, circumstances, and personal destiny.
my_opinion: Very good, down to the basics manual for life.

author: Daniel Kahneman
title: Thinking, Fast and Slow
why_read: Explores the dual systems driving human thought—fast intuition vs. deliberate logic—and exposes ubiquitous cognitive biases.
my_opinion: Super-interesting. Most widely applicable being part 1. A bit slow on the reading as its dense and longwinded, but worth every bit of information.

author: Nassim Nicholas Taleb
title: Antifragile: Things That Gain from Disorder
why_read: Introduces the concept of antifragility—systems and mindsets that thrive and grow stronger from shocks, volatility, and stress.

author: Irene Vallejo
title: El infinito en un junco
why_read: Un ensayo lírico y deslumbrante sobre la apasionante invención y supervivencia de los libros y bibliotecas en el mundo antiguo.

author: N/A
title: The New Testament
why_read: Central text of Christian ethics, narrative, and theology whose parables and moral teachings fundamentally shaped Western civilization.

author: Susanna Clarke
title: Piranesi
why_read: A poetic, haunting mystery following an innocent protagonist exploring an infinite, tide-swept house filled with statues.

author: Aristóteles
title: Retórica
why_read: El tratado fundamental sobre el arte de la persuasión, estructurado en torno al ethos (carácter), pathos (emoción) y logos (lógica).

author: Platón
title: República
why_read: El diálogo clásico más influyente sobre la justicia, el alma humana, la educación y la estructura del Estado ideal.
my_opinion: Incredible exercise, beautiful, amazing how current something still are, like the presence of drones in the democratic governments.

author: Niccolò Machiavelli
title: El príncipe
why_read: Un análisis descarnado y pragmático sobre cómo se adquiere, ejerce y retiene el poder político en el mundo real.

author: Santa Teresa de Jesús
title: Camino de Perfección
why_read: Guía práctica y cercana sobre la oración, el recogimiento interior, la humildad y la vida contemplativa.
my_opinion: Un poco redicho y antiguo el lenguaje. Pero muy interesante, ver cómo lideraba Sta Teresa, y cómo se parece a la meditación. La importancia de la humildad, y su lectura del Padre Nuestro.

author: Nassim Nicholas Taleb
title: The Black Swan
why_read: Examines highly improbable, massive-impact events and humanity's chronic blindness to randomness and uncertainty.

author: James MacGregor Burns
title: Transforming Leadership
why_read: A seminal study distinguishing transactional management from transformational leadership that elevates leaders and followers alike.

author: Sharon L. Bowman
title: Training from the Back of the Room!
why_read: Applies cognitive neuroscience to interactive, learner-centered teaching techniques that replace passive lectures.

author: John Doerr
title: Measure What Matters
why_read: The definitive guide to Objectives and Key Results (OKRs), showing how companies achieve focused execution and alignment.

author: Frédéric Laloux
title: Reinventing Organizations
why_read: Surveys the emergence of 'Teal' organizations characterized by self-management, wholeness, and evolutionary purpose.

author: Stephen Denning
title: The Leader's Guide to Storytelling
why_read: Explains how leaders can use narrative and storytelling strategically to spark action, foster collaboration, and transmit values.

author: David Rock
title: Your Brain at Work
why_read: Translates brain science into strategies for staying calm under pressure, overcoming distraction, and maximizing focus.

author: Jacqueline Brassey, Aaron De Smet & Michiel Kruyt
title: Deliberate Calm - How to Lead and Learn in a Volatile World
why_read: Combines neuroscience and behavioral psychology to help leaders maintain clarity, emotional composure, and adaptability in crisis.

author: Eliyahu M. Goldratt
title: Beyond the Goal
why_read: A comprehensive audio lecture series detailing the evolution and holistic application of the Theory of Constraints.

author: Emmanuel Carrère
title: L'Adversaire
why_read: Un estremecedor relato de no ficción sobre el caso de Jean-Claude Romand, quien engañó a su entorno durante 18 años antes de cometer una tragedia.

author: Paul Auster
why_read: Follows four parallel, alternate life trajectories of the same protagonist growing up during mid-20th century America.
my_opinion: Precioso libro, magistralmente escrito, con el marco de la américa (NY) de los años 60, 70, 80. Una maravilla para disfrutar.

author: Homer
title: La Iliada
why_read: El poema épico fundacional sobre la cólera de Aquiles, la tragedia de la guerra de Troya y la condición mortal humana.
my_opinion: A must read, second time around.

author: Homer
title: La Odisea
why_read: La gran epopeya del viaje de regreso de Odiseo a Ítaca, cargada de ingenio, peligros míticos y perseverancia.
my_opinion: A must read, second time around.

author: Joseph Heller
title: Catch-22
genre: fiction, novel, satirical war novel, classics, comedy
why_read: A devastatingly funny and profound critique of military bureaucracy, insanity, and the paradoxes of war.
my_opinion: Beautiful book, starts hilarious and non-sensical, and starts showing the drama of war, its effect on people, and the desertion of the state to its soldiers.

author: Ernest Hemingway
title: For Whom the Bell Tolls
why_read: A gripping tale of duty, camaraderie, and love set among anti-fascist guerrillas during the Spanish Civil War.
my_opinion: Beautifully writen, also a good look into our recen Spanish history. The senseless war, brutality, love, and beautiful narration.

author: Jordan B. Peterson
title: 12 Rules for Life: An Antidote to Chaos
why_read: Draws on clinical psychology, mythology, and religion to provide practical rules for taking personal responsibility in a chaotic world.
my_opinion: Nice set of rules and beautiful essays within touching on tangent points. A bit too heavy on the religious catholic background, but its substantiated and correct without falling too much on using it as a crutch to support his way of thinking.

author: Thich Nhat Hanh
title: Fear: Essential Wisdom for Getting Through the Storm
why_read: Gentle Buddhist teachings and practices for acknowledging deep-rooted fears and cultivating presence, peace, and release.

author: Tad Williams
title: Otherland (Tetralogy)
why_read: A monumental sci-fi epic where characters enter a vast, hyper-immersive virtual reality simulation harboring dark secrets.

author: Peter C. Brown, Henry L. Roediger III & Mark A. McDaniel
title: Make It Stick: The Science of Successful Learning
why_read: Debunks popular but ineffective study habits, offering scientifically proven methods like spaced retrieval and interleaved practice.
my_opinion: https://www.amazon.com/Make-Stick-Peter-Brown-Paperback/dp/B0CCCMPBV8?crid=UF39P2MHJ7C5&keywords=make+it+stick&qid=1690839988&sprefix=make+it+stick,aps,164&sr=8-1&linkCode=sl1&tag=flickthrough-20&linkId=e80c65c0853f6383b3db52c45cfaf0c1&language=en_US&ref_=as_li_ss_tl

author: Allen B. Downey
title: Think Stats: Exploratory Data Analysis in Python
why_read: An introduction to probability and statistics emphasized through computational methods and hands-on Python code rather than abstract math.
my_opinion: https://greenteapress.com/thinkstats2/html

author: Dante Alighieri
title: La divina comedia
why_read: Una obra cumbre de la literatura universal que narra un viaje alegórico a través del Infierno, el Purgatorio y el Paraíso.
my_opinion: Es realmente sorprendente cómo está hecho, y los temas que toca así como la forma de abordarlos. Sin embargo sin ser un gran conocedor de la historia del renacimiento italiano ni un gran conocedor de teología cristiana, se hace un poco árido. También pierde claramente con las traducciones.

author: Yuval Noah Harari
title: Sapiens: A Brief History of Humankind
why_read: A sweeping narrative of how shared fictions and cognitive revolutions allowed Homo sapiens to dominate planet Earth.
my_opinion: Explora hipotesis de las razones detrás de los mayores cambios en la historia de la humanidad. Cómo las construcciones mentales han sido el centro que ha permitido a la humanidad crear agrupaciones cada vez mayores, dentro de estos constructos, la religión, el capitalismo, la ciencia y su interrelación.

author: Carlo Rovelli
title: Seven Brief Lessons on Physics
why_read: Lyrical, accessible essays introducing relativity, quantum mechanics, black holes, and our place in the cosmos.

author: Jared Diamond
title: Why Is Sex Fun? The Evolution of Human Sexuality
why_read: An evolutionary examination of why human reproductive physiology and sexual behaviors differ radically from all other mammals.

author: Jared Diamond
title: Guns, Germs, and Steel: The Fates of Human Societies
why_read: Argues that environmental and geographical factors, not biological superiority, shaped the unequal development of civilizations.

author: Richard Dawkins
title: The God Delusion
why_read: A spirited evolutionary biologist's critique of religious faith and defense of rational scientific inquiry.

author: Richard Dawkins
title: The Selfish Gene
why_read: Revolutionized evolutionary biology by arguing that natural selection operates at the level of the gene rather than the individual.

author: Seneca
title: El libro de Oro
why_read: Antología clásica de sentencias morales y reflexiones estoicas de Séneca sobre la serenidad, la brevedad de la vida y la virtud.
my_opinion: Libro que recoge muchas frases cortas de la sabiduría de Seneca. Mucho para aprovechar.

author: Michael Wisehart
title: The Four-Part Key (The Aldoran Chronicles, Book 3)
why_read: Third installment in an epic fantasy series continuing the struggle against dark forces with complex magic systems and multiple POVs.
my_opinion: Dejo la serie es demasiado infantil.

author: Michael Wisehart
title: The White Tower (The Aldoran Chronicles, Book 1)
why_read: Opens an epic fantasy saga centered on forbidden magic, tyrannical religious regimes, and reluctant heroes.

author: Michael Wisehart
title: Plague of Shadows (The Aldoran Chronicles, Book 2)
why_read: Continues the Aldoran saga as the young wielders of magic confront political intrigue and impending darkness.

author: James Clear
title: Atomic Habits: Tiny Changes, Remarkable Results
why_read: A highly practical blueprint for creating good habits, breaking bad ones, and harnessing the power of 1% incremental progress.

author: José Luis Corral
title: Independencia
why_read: Novela histórica ambientada en los heroicos y dramáticos sitios de Zaragoza durante la Guerra de la Independencia Española.
my_opinion: Libro interesantillo por lo que toca la historia de Zaragoza, pero póbremente escrito con muy muy poco gancho

author: Marcus Tullius Cicero
title: Tusculanae Disputationes
why_read: Diálogos filosóficos donde Cicerón reflexiona sobre el desprecio a la muerte, el alivio del dolor y cómo la virtud basta para la felicidad.

author: Jiddu Krishnamurti
title: Freedom from the Known
why_read: A radical invitation to free the mind from psychological conditioning, dogmas, and the illusion of the separate ego.
my_opinion: Very deep and good book, but difficult to really follow forcing you to think rather than giving answers.

author: Jiddu Krishnamurti
title: Discover the Immeasurable (Talks in Germany)
why_read: Spoken talks exploring choiceless awareness, the ending of psychological fear, and perceiving truth beyond thought.
my_opinion: Very nice book on the observations of JK, how to move from the known and what is needed to be able to perceive what there is of "godlike" or Religious in us. A process of observation, and freedom from conditioning external and internal.

author: Nnedi Okorafor
title: Binti: The Complete Trilogy
why_read: A vibrant novella series blending Himba cultural traditions with interstellar adventure, alien diplomacy, and identity.
my_opinion: Nice and entertaining novel, full of imagination and easy to read.

author: Ajahn Chah
title: Food for the Heart: The Collected Teachings of Ajahn Chah
why_read: Simple, direct, and witty Dhamma talks from the revered Thai Forest Tradition master on impermanence and non-attachment.
my_opinion: About budism and its practice. Beautiful book to learn in a very clear way what the practice is. Clear guidance and counsel

author: Tamas Bodzsar
title: The Rhythm Code
why_read: A structured methodology for musicians and students to intuitively decode, internalize, and master complex rhythmic patterns.
my_opinion: Learning about music rhythm, a system to understanding rhythm

author: Kosho Uchiyama
title: Opening the Hand of Thought: Foundations of Zen Buddhist Practice
why_read: A profound Soto Zen guide that strips away exoticism to present zazen as simply letting go of thoughts and returning to reality.
my_opinion: Zazen learning

author: Brandon Sanderson
title: Wind and Truth (The Stormlight Archive, Book 5)
why_read: The climactic conclusion to the first five-book arc of the Stormlight Archive, delivering monumental battles and character payoffs.
my_opinion: Fantasy, fiction novel

author: Ursula K. Le Guin
title: A Wizard of Earthsea
why_read: A beautifully written masterpiece about balance, pride, naming magic, and confronting the shadow within oneself.
my_opinion: Rereading a classic of fantasy

author: Ursula K. Le Guin
title: The Tombs of Atuan
why_read: A claustrophobic, atmospheric story of a young high priestess finding liberation from ancient dark cults.
my_opinion: Rereading a classic of fantasy

author: Ursula K. Le Guin
title: The Farthest Shore
why_read: An elegiac voyage across Earthsea investigating the loss of magic, the dread of death, and the restoration of life's balance.
my_opinion: Rereading a classic of fantasy

author: Rupert Spira
title: Being Aware of Being Aware
why_read: A clear, accessible introduction to the direct path of recognizing pure awareness as the essential nature of experience.
my_opinion: Meditation, awareness, good book explaining to occidentals what awareness is and its characteristics

author: Thich Nhat Hanh
title: The Miracle of Mindfulness
why_read: A warm, practical manual showing how everyday tasks like washing dishes or peeling an orange become profound acts of meditation.
my_opinion: Rereading this book. Meditation learning, perhaps one of the best books I have read on this.

author: Jane Austen
title: Pride and Prejudice
why_read: Austen's most sparkling, witty novel satirizing social expectations, pride, and the perils of quick judgment.
my_opinion: Beautifull prose, marvellous dialogues and costumbrist picture of a place and an era.

author: Sam Harris
title: Waking Up: A Guide to Spirituality Without Religion
why_read: Bridges secular neuroscience and contemplative insights, showing how self-transcendence is verifiable without religious dogma.
my_opinion: Secular meditation and consciousness exploration. Great balance of science and insight.

author: Michael A. Singer
title: The Untethered Soul: The Journey Beyond Yourself
why_read: Teaches how to step back as the witness of your own thoughts, release emotional energy blockages, and live in freedom.
my_opinion: I like much better how it starts than how it ends. It is a very interesting book that focuses on awareness and explains things in a nice clear way on how to progress to bring yourself closer to enlightenment, but as you approach the end the practical suggestions on how to proceed start dissapearing and becomes more vague. I think it is very good nonetheless, and explains in a practical way things to people who have not even meditated before. I have liked it, enjoyed it, I think I have learned from it, but at some point I expected a bit more out of it. It gets on to preaching moralism somehow, describing the wonderful things that you will achieve if you reach this state, rather than the how and the logic behing them, and blatantly tries to capture Christian, Bible lovers trying to bring them under its wing, and i felt this was incredibly unnecesary and out of place.

author: Ichiro Kishimi & Fumitake Koga
title: The Courage to Be Disliked
why_read: Presents Adlerian psychology in a Socratic dialogue, demonstrating how true freedom comes from separating life tasks and accepting dislike.
my_opinion: Dialogued format exploring freedom, acceptance, and personal responsibility.

author: Seneca
title: Letters from a Stoic
why_read: Warm, practical letters offering guidance on dealing with grief, friendship, aging, wealth, and living a virtuous life.
my_opinion: More personal and emotionally rich than Cicero. Ideal for daily philosophical reflection.

author: Jon Kabat-Zinn
title: Wherever You Go, There You Are
why_read: Bite-sized, poetic reflections that bring the essence of mindfulness meditation into daily domestic and working life.
my_opinion: Secular, poetic, and accessible introduction to mindfulness in everyday life.

author: Viktor E. Frankl
title: Man's Search for Meaning
why_read: A profound testimony of surviving Nazi concentration camps that introduces logotherapy—the pursuit of meaning as life's primary drive.
my_opinion: Short and powerful; blends psychology, suffering, and purpose. A modern classic. The first half is powerful, mostly because it does not show hatred, and judges as equanimously as could be wished. The second half gives a certain depth, even if it feels a bit like banging his own drum, it supports and builds on the first half of the book.

author: Ryan Holiday
title: The Obstacle Is the Way
why_read: Applies Marcus Aurelius's Stoic formula—turning trials into triumphs—through historical anecdotes of great leaders.
my_opinion: Modern take on Stoicism; clear, actionable, and motivating. I didnt enjoy it so much though, I think it is a nice reflection but I dont really think there is so much content in it. It is a good read all in all though. I think well worth the time. But not entirely sure it adds many novel ideas, rather collects existing thoughts presenting examples.

author: Shunryu Suzuki
title: Zen Mind, Beginner's Mind
why_read: A beloved Zen classic emphasizing 'beginner's mind'—an attitude of openness, curiosity, and freedom from preconceptions.
my_opinion: Beautiful, beautiful, personal, direct touch on meditation and zen, already read it twice, probably will come back to it yet again.

author: Thich Nhat Hanh
title: The Art of Communicating
why_read: Shows how deep compassionate listening and loving speech can heal misunderstandings and transform relationships.
my_opinion: Another beautiful book by Thich, I really like it somethings I want to explore like some of the mantras, some others seem a bit difficult to put into practice, but all in all its very good reading

author: R. F. Kuang
title: The Poppy War
why_read: A brutal, dark fantasy inspired by 20th-century Chinese history and the Opium Wars, exploring shamanism, war, and vengeance.
my_opinion: Entertaining, nice and quick narration.

author: R. F. Kuang
title: The Dragon Republic (The Poppy War, Book 2)
why_read: The second chapter of Rin's story dealing with civil war, political betrayal, and the devastating cost of divine wrath.
my_opinion: Entertaining, nice and quick narration.

author: R. F. Kuang
title: The Burning God (The Poppy War, Book 3)
why_read: The blistering finale of the trilogy as Rin fights for the southern provinces and faces the ultimate consequence of absolute power.
my_opinion: Entertaining, nice and quick narration.

author: Mark Manson
title: The Subtle Art of Not Giving a F*ck
why_read: A blunt, counter-intuitive self-help guide advocating that happiness comes from choosing what struggles and values actually matter to you.
my_opinion: About life, in funny learnings from someone that looked like he had THE life.

author: Confucius
title: The Analects of Confucius
why_read: Foundational aphorisms of Confucian philosophy focused on ritual propriety, filial piety, benevolence, and virtuous rule.
my_opinion: Some very interesting pearls of wisdom, much in the style of Seneca I think. It must have been such an interesting character.

author: Felix Adler
title: The Essentials of Spirituality
why_read: Articulates an ethical culture perspective connecting true spiritual growth to moral striving and elevating human dignity.
my_opinion: Very nice book, that proposes that spirituality is linked to upholding to high moral values and setting a continuous effort on upholding and improving on them through out your life.

author: Sun Tzu
title: The Art of War
why_read: Ancient Chinese military treatise on strategic advantage, deception, psychological discipline, and winning without fighting.
my_opinion: Interesting way of methodically taking at combat strategy. Somewhat applicable i guess to modern day company work strategy, but I dont really see how to do it in a direct way. I do love however how the author took to detailing and taking the thought structure appart.

author: St. George Stock
title: A Guide to Stoicism
why_read: A concise historical overview tracing the origins, logic, physics, and ethics of the ancient Greek and Roman Stoics.
my_opinion: Somewhat dull introduction to stoicism where much more import is given to the history of it as a philosophy than to the actual tenants of the philosophy, i havent really appreciated it.

author: Pierce Brown
title: Red Rising
why_read: A fast-paced, visceral dystopian sci-fi novel about a lowborn miner infiltrating Mars' ruling elite to ignite a revolution.
my_opinion: Nicely paced science fiction novel, much in the distopian young adult kind of line as hunger games and others. Pulling a lot from the Lord of the flies and Orson Scott Caard, Enders Game

author: Stephen R. Covey
title: The 7 Habits of Highly Effective People
why_read: A principle-centered approach to personal and professional effectiveness based on character ethics rather than superficial techniques.

author: Oscar Wilde
title: The Picture of Dorian Gray
why_read: Wilde's cautionary aesthetic tale of vanity, hedonism, and moral decay centered on an ageless young man and his aging portrait.
my_opinion: Beautifully written, nice to read the origins of gothic horror in such a delightful way. Beautiful dialogues and corruption

author: Clayton M. Christensen
title: The Innovator's Dilemma: When New Technologies Cause Great Firms to Fail
why_read: A landmark business study explaining how market leaders get blindsided and displaced by cheaper, disruptive technologies.

author: Jim Clifton & Jim Harter
title: It's the Manager: Moving From Boss to Coach
why_read: Backed by massive Gallup workplace research, reveals that a company's success or failure depends mostly on the quality of its managers.

author: Sönke Ahrens
title: How to Take Smart Notes
why_read: The definitive English guide to the Zettelkasten slip-box note-taking method, turning reading and thinking into effortless writing.

author: Sun Tzu
title: The Art of War
why_read: Timeless strategic insights on preparation, adaptability, and positioning applicable to management and conflict resolution.
my_opinion: Nice how it analices in a methodical way the things to keep in mind for war, and the thought process as a leader

author: Ryan Holiday & Stephen Hanselman
title: The Daily Stoic: 366 Meditations on Wisdom, Perseverance, and the Art of Living
why_read: Offers daily bite-sized translations and commentary from Marcus Aurelius, Seneca, and Epictetus for everyday contemplation.

author: Felix Adler
title: The Essentials of Spirituality
why_read: Explores how devotion to moral ideals and social duty can form the foundation of a profound non-theistic spiritual life.
my_opinion: Beautiful book on what spirituality means, and some very good guidance on how to work on it, what to focus on.

author: Lysandra Wren
title: The Adler Awakening
why_read: A direct summary of core Adlerian psychological principles: shedding past trauma identity, choosing future goals, and contributing to community.
my_opinion: To the point, not a great book, but great concepts: 1 let go of past as your identity. 2 Move goals to focus and future direction 3 Act from inspiration instead of fear 4 Contribute socially rather than staying in self-protection 5 Live authentically, not by approval 6 Intentionally create your future self 7 Avoid introspection loops and brokenness thinking 8 Reclaim agency through purposeful choices

author: Fyodor Dostoevsky
title: Notes from the House of the Dead
why_read: Based on Dostoevsky's Siberian prison labor, a penetrating portrait of convicts, human nature, despair, and freedom.
my_opinion: Sensible perceptions of peoples characters, motivations, and feeling of what prison life is and what it implies for the prisoner

author: Patricia B. McConnell
title: The Other End of the Leash: Why We Do What We Do Around Dogs
why_read: An applied animal behaviorist explains how primate human gestures differ from canine body language, transforming human-dog communication.
my_opinion: Beautifull book for dog lovers, nice intro to dogs Ethology.

author: Aldous Huxley
title: Brave New World
why_read: A chilling prophecy of a society controlled not by pain or fear, but by pleasure, conditioned conformity, and technological distraction.
my_opinion: Beautifully written with great ideas, presented in an intelligent and attractive fashion. Good way to present some of the trends in our current culture and making it clear they lead to childish unresponsible being.

author: Carl G. Jung
title: Man and His Symbols
why_read: Jung's only popular work written for general readers, explaining the unconscious mind, dreams, archetypes, and individuation.

author: Joshua Kingsman
title: Carl Jung Explained: His Core Theories, Books & Influence
why_read: An accessible, introductory overview of Jung's key concepts—the shadow, anima/animus, archetypes, and synchronicity.
my_opinion: Ok introduction to Carl Jung, it explains concepts clearly and how they fit on Jungs life. Its a nice introduction to get deeper afterwards.

author: William Shakespeare
title: A Midsummer Night's Dream
why_read: Shakespeare's enchanting comedy of magical mix-ups, fairy interference, and the follies of romantic love in an enchanted forest.

author: Antoine de Saint-Exupéry
title: Le Petit Prince
why_read: Un cuento poético e inolvidable sobre el amor, la amistad y la pérdida, recordándonos que sólo con el corazón se puede ver bien.
my_opinion: Beautifully crafted text to get back to your inner child. To review whats important without getting into the reasoning, but getting to you through strong emotions. Love every bit of it.

author: Fyodor Dostoevsky
title: The Brothers Karamazov
why_read: A towering masterpiece of world literature interrogating faith, doubt, morality, and patricide through four passionately divergent brothers.
my_opinion: Beautiful Book Incredible Written, The depth of the characters, the richness of the dialogues the wideness of the views, how he treats religion and spirituality. I particularly liked the chapter in which event talks to the what he figures is the devil, I had such fun with that chapter. I feel like Dostoievaky really enjoyed writing that part. I have really enjoyed and love this book. it has a certain depth and philosophy to it, trying to take different sites to win that proving his point but not belittling the other positions

author: Robert A. Johnson
title: Inner Work: Using Dreams and Active Imagination for Personal Growth
why_read: A clear, four-step guide for working safely with your own dreams and active imagination to integrate unconscious wisdom.

author: Donald Robertson
title: How to Think Like a Roman Emperor: The Stoic Philosophy of Marcus Aurelius
genre: stoicism, cognitive behavioral therapy, self-help, philosophy
why_read: Integrates Marcus Aurelius's life and Stoic wisdom with modern cognitive behavioral therapy techniques for emotional resilience.

author: Ichiro Kishimi & Fumitake Koga
title: The Courage to Be Happy
why_read: The sequel to The Courage to Be Disliked, focusing on how to actually live Adlerian principles of love, friendship, and self-reliance daily.

author: Robin Hobb
title: Ship of Magic (Liveship Traders, Book 1)
genre: fantasy, nautical fantasy, epic fantasy, novel
why_read: First book of the acclaimed Liveship Traders trilogy, featuring sentient wooden ships, seafaring politics, and rich character growth.

author: Ernest Becker
title: The Denial of Death
why_read: Pulitzer Prize-winning work arguing that human civilization is largely an elaborate defense mechanism against the terror of mortality.

author: Shinzen Young
title: The Science of Enlightenment: How Meditation Works
why_read: A rigorous, systematic exploration unifying ancient contemplative techniques with modern scientific clarity.
my_opinion: Algorithmic and logical approach to meditation. High precision in describing sensory clarity and equanimity.

author: Greg Goode
title: The Direct Path: A User Guide
why_read: A hands-on, experiment-based guide using direct sensory inquiry to dissolve the perceived boundary between subject and object.
my_opinion: Technical user guide for non-dual investigation. Focuses on the lack of boundary between observer and observed through logical experiments.

author: SenLinYu
title: Alchemised
genre: dark fantasy, dystopian, romance, fiction, novel
why_read: A dark, atmospheric fantasy exploring trauma, survival, memory manipulation, and healing in the wake of a devastating war.
my_opinion: Ok story, but way to young adult in how flat or one sided every character seems to be. The world and magic are what I liked the best. I finished it I guess because I had purchased it as an audiobook and it kept me company, but it was a bit too young for me without anything to dream about wild thoughts (other than the magic system that at some point just kind of ... meh!

author: James Joyce
title: Ulysses
why_read: A monumental landmark of modernist literature chronicling one single day in Dublin through groundbreaking linguistic innovation.

author: Christopher Buehlman
title: The Blacktongue Thief
why_read: A witty, grimy, fast-moving fantasy told in the distinctive voice of a nimble thief bound to a perilous quest.
my_opinion: Witty, funny, makes you love the characters, development and fast pace without looking like you are on a superficial action packed loop. I will continue to read the saga as its produced.

author: Jay Kristoff
